title: Feelings and Calm Bodies
bigQuestion: What can we do when big feelings show up in our bodies?

story.title: Balloon Breathing
story.kicker: Before a spelling test, Jamal's tummy feels tight, and his teacher shows him a trick.
paragraphs: It was Friday. Spelling test day. Jamal sat at his desk. His tummy felt tight, like a fist. His hands felt sweaty.
Ms. Lee knelt by his desk. "You look worried," she said softly. Jamal nodded. "My tummy feels funny." Ms. Lee said, "Let's try balloon breathing."
"Put your hands on your tummy," she said. "Breathe in slowly through your nose. Fill your tummy like a balloon. Now let the air out slowly."
Jamal did it three times. His tummy felt softer. His hands felt calm. He picked up his pencil. He was ready to try.
story.think: Where in his body did Jamal feel his worry?

lessons.title: Many Feelings
lessons.mainIdea: Everyone has many feelings, and we can name them.
reading: You wake up and it snows. You feel happy. Your friend moves away. You feel sad. Someone takes your toy. You feel mad.
A *feeling* is what is going on inside you. Happy, sad, mad, scared and worried are all feelings. Every feeling is okay to have.

words.d: what is going on inside you, like happy, sad or mad

look.title: Faces
look.text: Look at three faces. One has a big smile. One has tears on the cheeks. One has tight lips and a wrinkled forehead.
look.prompt: What feeling does each face show?

check.q: Your friend moves away. How might you feel?
check.why: The reading says you might feel sad when a friend moves away.

check.q: Which one is a feeling?
check.why: Worried is a feeling, like happy or scared.

check.q: Are all feelings okay to have?
check.why: The reading says every feeling is okay to have.

lessons.title: Scared and Worried
lessons.mainIdea: Being scared or worried is a way our body tries to keep us safe.
reading: A big dog barks. You jump back. You feel *scared*. Being scared can help you stay away from danger.
*Worried* is a feeling about something that might happen. You may worry about a test or a new class. Worry often gets smaller when you talk about it.

words.d: a feeling that something might hurt you
a feeling of thinking about something that might go wrong

look.title: First Day
look.text: It is Rosa's first day at a new school. She does not know anyone yet. She keeps thinking, What if nobody plays with me?
look.prompt: What feeling does Rosa have? Who could she talk to?

check.q: What is worry about?

check.q: What often makes worry smaller?
check.why: The reading says worry often gets smaller when you talk about it.

lessons.title: Body Clues
lessons.mainIdea: Feelings show up in our bodies, and we can notice the clues.
reading: Feelings do not stay only in your head. When you are mad, your face may get hot. When you are worried, your tummy may feel tight.
These are *body clues*. When you are scared, your heart may beat fast. Noticing a clue helps you know what you feel.

words.d: a sign in your body that shows a feeling, like a tight tummy

lessons.title: Everyone's Brain Is Different
lessons.mainIdea: Every brain works in its own way, and that is okay.
reading: Your *brain* helps you think and feel. Every brain works in its own way. Some kids like quiet. Some kids like to move while they learn.
Loud sounds may bother one kid and not another. One kid may need a break. Another may need a hug. Knowing what helps you is a strength.

words.d: the part inside your head that helps you think, feel and move

look.text: At a birthday party, Ben laughs and jumps near the loud music. His friend Ava puts on soft earmuffs and sits in a quiet corner with a book.

check.why: Every brain works in its own way.

check.q: What is a strength?
check.why: The reading says knowing what helps you is a strength.

lessons.title: Calm Breathing
lessons.mainIdea: Slow breathing can help a body feel calm.
reading: Try this. Pretend to smell a flower. Breathe in slowly through your nose. Now pretend to blow out a candle. Breathe out slowly.
This is *calm breathing*. Slow breaths tell your body it is safe. Your heart can slow down. Your tummy can feel softer.

words.d: breathing in and out slowly to help your body relax

look.title: Flower and Candle
look.text: Hold up one finger like a flower. Smell it slowly. Now pretend your finger is a candle. Blow out the flame softly. Do it three times.
look.prompt: How does your body feel after three slow breaths?

check.q: In calm breathing, what do you pretend to smell?
check.why: You pretend to smell a flower as you breathe in.

check.q: How should you breathe out?
check.why: You breathe out slowly, like blowing out a candle.

check.q: What do slow breaths tell your body?
check.why: Slow breaths tell your body it is safe.

lessons.title: Stretching and Quiet Time
lessons.mainIdea: Stretching and quiet time can help a busy body rest.
reading: Reach your arms up high like a tall tree. Now bend and touch your toes. *Stretching* helps tight muscles let go.
*Quiet time* helps too. You can sit in a cozy corner. You can look at a book or listen to soft music. A few quiet minutes can help you feel ready again.

words.d: reaching and bending your body slowly to loosen your muscles
a few calm minutes to rest your body and mind

check.q: What does stretching help?

check.q: What can you do in quiet time?
check.why: In quiet time you can look at a book or listen to soft music.

check.q: How can a few quiet minutes help?
choices: They help you feel ready again
check.why: The reading says quiet minutes can help you feel ready again.

lessons.title: Asking for Help
lessons.mainIdea: When a feeling is too big, ask a trusted adult for help.
reading: Sometimes a feeling is too big to handle alone. That is okay. You can ask for *help*.
Tell a trusted adult. That could be a parent, a teacher or the school counselor. You can say, "I feel worried. Can we talk?" Sharing a feeling can make it lighter.

words.d: support from someone when something is hard
a school helper who listens and helps kids with feelings

look.title: Who Can Help?
look.text: Make a list of grown-ups who help you. Maybe a mom or dad. Maybe a grandma. Maybe your teacher. Maybe the school counselor.

choices: Ask a trusted adult for help
check.why: The reading says you can ask a trusted adult for help.

check.q: Who is a school helper for feelings?
check.why: A counselor listens and helps kids with feelings.

check.q: What can sharing a feeling do?
check.why: Sharing a feeling can make it lighter.

lessons.title: Kindness Helps Everyone
lessons.mainIdea: Kind words and actions help everyone feel safe.
reading: Mia saw a boy sitting alone at lunch. She sat down and said, "Hi, want to share my grapes?" The boy smiled.
That was *kindness*. Kind words and actions help people feel safe. When we feel safe, our bodies feel calmer. Kindness helps the helper feel good too.

words.d: being friendly, caring and helpful to others

look.title: Kind or Not?
look.text: One kid laughs when a friend drops her tray. Another kid helps her pick it up and says, "That happens to everyone."
look.prompt: Which kid showed kindness? How might the friend feel?

check.q: What did Mia do that was kind?

check.why: Mia sat down and shared her grapes.

check.q: How do kind actions help people?
check.why: Kind words and actions help people feel safe.

check.q: Who feels good when you are kind?

check.why: The reading says kindness helps the helper feel good too.
